name: Publications / Public Read and Crawler Ingestion

access.anon: May read published news and notices, including verified linked media and attachments; cannot write or inspect crawler ingestion data.
access.user: May use the same anonymous public read surface. Crawler writes use a dedicated Worker secret and are not user-authenticated.
access.admin: May read the public surface. The publication crawler is a machine principal authenticated by a dedicated Worker secret.
access.agent: A crawler submits REST ingestion requests with the X-Publication-Ingestion-Secret header. Public reads are anonymous REST/Web capabilities; ingestion remains a REST-only crawler exception and is not a Web, GraphQL, or MCP capability.

rules.public-read: Anonymous reads expose only non-deleted publications whose effective type is news or notice. The list supports optional type=news|notice, source, query, page, and pageSize filters; detail addresses are public by publication id. Deleted publications and other are never returned by this surface.
rules.reprint-folding: news.ustc.edu.cn republishes one article under multiple section canonical URLs, each a distinct legitimate Publication row. The list accepts an opt-in fold=1 parameter that groups rows by (normalized title, published date in Asia/Shanghai) and returns one representative per group, preferring a university organizationLevel source, else the most recently seen copy, then the lowest id. Folding defaults to off; making it the list default is an open product question.
rules.reprint-fold-title-normalization: Fold grouping keys on a normalized title: NFKC normalization, invisible-character stripping, whitespace collapsing and lowercasing, implemented by normalizePublicationTitle() in src/features/publications/lib/publication-title-normalization.ts and mirrored by a Postgres generated column so grouping runs in SQL rather than in application memory. The helper and the column must change together.
rules.reprint-sibling-exposure: A folded row representing two or more members carries foldGroup.siblingCount; an unfolded request never includes foldGroup. Independent of fold, the detail response always includes alsoPublishedIn, the sibling reprints sharing the same normalized title and published date, so a detail page can cross-link the other sections.
rules.public-object-read: A private R2 object is readable only when its content-addressed key is tied to a linked or verified object and an object link on a non-tombstone revision of a non-deleted news or notice publication. The Worker checks this relationship before reading R2; missing objects return not found and metadata reads do not fail ingestion.
rules.publication-markdown: Crawler revisions may link a body_markdown object. The public detail read loads that object from R2 and returns bodyMarkdown explicitly as a string, empty string, or null when no verified current object is available; it never substitutes bodyText. body_html remains an unchanged archive object.
rules.publication-images: Ingestion registers exact source URL SHA-256 hashes for current public revisions. Markdown uses /api/publications/images/{hash}. Fetches and redirects allow the registered exact public hostname, USTC and source allowed hosts; blocked hosts win. IP/local hosts, credentials, custom ports, non-HTTP(S), non-raster and oversized responses are rejected. Successful images are archived in R2 with finite response cache lifetimes; failures are not cached.
rules.public-cache: Public list/detail responses are cacheable JSON. Object responses use their content-addressed key as a long-lived immutable cache key and forward a provider ETag for conditional requests. Media may render inline; all other object kinds use a generated safe attachment filename and never trust crawler-provided filenames.
rules.rest-only: Publication ingestion and object upload planning are exposed only under /api/ingestion/publications. Do not add Web, GraphQL, or MCP transports for these writes, and do not treat the machine secret as a user OAuth credential.
rules.read-transport-boundary: The current product needs a public website preview plus public REST for read/list/detail and controlled object delivery. GraphQL and MCP are intentionally not added for publications until a separate client contract requires them; this is a transport boundary, not an implicit GraphQL/MCP capability.
rules.service-auth: Ingestion writes require the X-Publication-Ingestion-Secret header, compared against the Worker secret PUBLICATION_INGESTION_SECRET with a timing-safe comparison. Missing or invalid configuration returns the same generic 401 response, and the secret is never logged or returned.
rules.service-principal: All crawler batches, runs, and object claims use the stable service:publication-crawler principal key. The service principal has no User row, OAuth grant, or administrator flag; this key scopes ownership and idempotency.
rules.source-registration: Every batch carries source descriptors, either the full id/name/organizationLevel/allowedHosts/seedUrls form or the minimal id/name form. The server upserts them in the same transaction, normalizing organizationLevel to the registry enum and reusing persisted host restrictions and the persisted level for minimal descriptors, then accepts an item only when its sourceId is in that batch, enabled and not discovery-only. Canonical URLs must match an allowed source host and no blocked host.
rules.identity: A publication is identified by (sourceId, canonicalUrl). A revision is identified by (publicationId, revisionHash), and each revision owns its object links.
rules.revision-ordering: observedAt is the source observation time. An older observation never overwrites the current revision; equal timestamps use the revision hash as a deterministic tie-breaker. A date-only or timezone-less crawler timestamp is interpreted as Asia/Shanghai local time before persistence.
rules.tombstones: Deletion is explicit: a tombstone item creates a tombstone revision for an existing publication and marks it deleted. Tombstoning an unknown publication is an idempotent no-op reported as unchanged with null publication and revision ids. A tombstone applied to an existing publication is reported as updated.
rules.batch-idempotency: Batch identity is scoped by principalKey and batchId. Replaying the same canonical payload returns the stored result without reapplying writes; reusing the pair with another digest returns 409. clientRunId is likewise scoped by principalKey.
rules.batch-size: A publication ingestion batch accepts 1-100 items. Larger batches are rejected by the request schema and must be split by the crawler before submission.
rules.partial-item-rejection: A source or item validation error is returned as a per-item rejected result and does not roll back other valid items in the batch. Batch-level identity, manifest, and database failures remain errors.
rules.objects: The server generates content-addressed keys; clients cannot choose keys or metadata. Manifests are at most 32 MiB. Metadata ingestion may precede the R2 object. Planning verifies size, content type, kind, SHA-256 metadata, and bytes (or a provider checksum), and immediately links an already-present object. An uploaded object must be verified and linked through complete.
rules.unchanged-objects: An unchanged item still re-registers its object claims against the current batch so a redelivery under a new batchId can plan uploads. When a claimed object has no verified bytes (status other than verified or linked), the item result carries objectsNeedingUpload entries ({ kind, sha256 }) and the client must plan and upload those objects against the new batchId; the field is absent when every claimed object is already verified.
rules.outbox: Accepted revisions write a durable PublicationEventOutbox row in the same transaction. A future Queue consumer may derive work from this outbox; the ingestion path does not claim delivery until a real publisher exists.
rules.content-type: Manifests require bare MIME types (for example text/html or image/png); parameters such as charset are rejected. For each (kind, sha256), the first PublicationObject contentType is canonical. Later manifests with the same kind, sha256, and size may use a MIME alias; r2Key and size stay strict. Batch claims, upload plans, presigned PUTs, and completion checks use canonical contentType. Revision replay compares object identity, size, role/order, and alt text, ignoring MIME aliases.
rules.required-upload-headers: An upload plan returns the exact required Content-Type, x-amz-meta-kind, and x-amz-meta-sha256 headers. Presigned URLs are short-lived and no R2 credentials are returned.
rules.source-registry: PublicationSource is the registry of who publishes. organizationLevel is a closed enum (university, office, department, college, center, research, service, program, society, journal, student, unknown) whose declaration order is the directory's display order. The crawler owns the upstream vocabulary, so ingestion normalizes an unrecognized or absent level to unknown instead of rejecting the batch. The directory lists enabled, non-discovery-only sources, including one that has published nothing yet.

publication-read.title: Public publication list, detail, and verified object read

notes: Defaults to non-deleted news and notices; optional type accepts only news or notice.
Supports source, query, page, and pageSize filters. query searches the indexed canonical URL, title, and summary fields; raw crawler metadata and archive HTML are never exposed.

Optional fold=1 (issue #1068, opt-in, default off) groups reprints of the same article across sections by normalized title and published date, returning one representative row per group with an optional foldGroup.siblingCount when the group has 2+ members.
Returns the effective current revision with its verified/linked object metadata. Deleted, tombstoned, and other publications are not found.
alsoPublishedIn always lists sibling publications sharing this article's normalized title and published date (see reprint-folding), independent of the list fold parameter.
The server derives and checks the R2 content-addressed key; clients cannot choose an arbitrary key.
Responses use ETag/immutable cache headers and safe content disposition.
Resolves only a hash linked to a current public news or notice revision from the ingestion imageSources map; there is no arbitrary URL proxy parameter.

Successful raster images are cached in R2 under a URL-hash namespace with finite cache headers because the upstream URL may change. Invalid origins, redirect targets, credentials, custom ports, private/local hosts, non-raster responses, oversized bodies, and origin failures are rejected without caching.

fields: current revision title, summary, bodyText, and source URL
current bodyMarkdown loaded from the body_markdown R2 object

notes: Request and response use the shared camelCase fixture shape in docs/contracts/fixtures/publication-batch.json.

Each non-tombstone item may include imageSources, mapping lowercase SHA-256(UTF-8 original absolute image URL) keys to original URLs; the server stores the map in the indexed image-source registry, and body_markdown Markdown must reference the same-origin /api/publications/images/{hash} paths.

Each result includes sourceId, canonicalUrl, and revisionHash so repeated URLs or revisions remain unambiguous. Status is created, updated, unchanged, or rejected; rejected results include an error and nullable publicationId/revisionId.

An unchanged result may include objectsNeedingUpload ({ kind, sha256 }[]) listing claimed objects whose bytes were never verified; the client plans and uploads those objects against the response batchId.
Only manifests registered by the caller's accepted batch may be planned.

Each object is already_present or upload_required. An already_present object is trusted from a prior verification (status verified or linked) without re-heading R2; upload_required includes the authenticated Worker uploadUrl, r2Key, and requiredHeaders.
The server resolves the key from the registered manifest, streams the body through the Worker R2 binding, and supplies the manifest SHA-256 to R2 for upload-time verification before linking it.

fields: content-addressed object manifest and verification status
